The ocarina is an aerophone of the vessel-flute class, H-S number 421.221.422. A typical instrument is a closed cavity with four to twelve fingerholes and a mouthpiece projecting from the body; it is traditionally made of clay or ceramic, and also of plastic, wood, glass, metal or bone. In playing, air passes the voicing and strikes the edge, and covering the holes changes pitch. Its forebears are found in Chinese and Mesoamerican cultures: the Maya and Aztecs used it for ornament and sacrifice, and it later reached Europe, where it served as a toy instrument, and in nineteenth-century Italy it developed into the modern ocarina.
橫吹式瓦卡通常呈圓形，演奏者雙手水平持握，將吹嘴對準唇部。氣流經風道撞擊唇片發聲: The transverse huaca is usually round; the player holds it horizontally in both hands and puts the mouthpiece to the lips. Air passes through the windway and strikes the lip to sound; covering a hole lowers the pitch and opening it raises it. A beginner first blows a steady, gentle stream to produce the fundamental, then opens the holes one by one following the scale. Because the force of the breath changes pitch directly, the fingers and the breath must be practised together, avoiding too strong or too weak a stream that would shift the intonation.

瓦卡屬氣鳴樂器，發聲靠氣流經吹嘴內導槽撞擊邊棱，再由壺狀腔體共振。其音色接近無泛: The huaca is an aerophone; it sounds when air passes the channel inside the mouthpiece, strikes the edge, and the vessel-shaped cavity resonates. Its timbre is close to having no overtones, because the Helmholtz resonator amplifies only the fundamental; the softness or hardness of the breath changes pitch rather than volume, so volume is hard to control and the fingerholes and breath must work together. Range is limited by the total area of the open holes; an alto in C can play a twelfth from A to F, and double and triple chambers extend it. Unlike long tube flutes, pitch depends on the ratio of open-hole area to cavity volume, and hole position matters less.
瓦卡所屬的陶笛家族歷史悠久，早期見於中國與中美洲文化。遠征中美洲後，阿茲特克人的: The ocarina family to which the huaca belongs has a long history, appearing early in Chinese and Mesoamerican cultures. After the expeditions to Mesoamerica, Aztec music and dance entered European courts and later became a toy. In the nineteenth century Giuseppe Donati in Italy developed it into a more complete instrument. In 1928 Aketagawa Takashi added two semitone holes to the ten-hole instrument, forming the twelve-hole pattern. In 1964 John Taylor extended the range with a four-hole fingering system.
瓦卡見於節慶、祭祀與儀式，也曾作為歐洲玩具樂器。二十世紀後進入管弦樂編制：匈牙利: The huaca appears at festivals, sacrifices and rituals, and also served as a European toy instrument. In the twentieth century it entered orchestral scoring: the Hungarian-Austrian composer Ligeti calls for four in his Violin Concerto, played by the woodwind players; the Polish composer Penderecki uses twelve in The Dream of Jacob and has fifty played by choir members at the end of his Eighth Symphony. The French composer Alvy wrote scores for it, and The Happy Ocarina was used on a BBC children's programme. It also appears today in game scores and on recital albums.
